paragraphs.sourceText: Thirst grows for living unplugged
paragraphs.translationZh: 对不插电生活的渴望与日俱增

paragraphs.sourceText: More people are taking breaks from the connected life amid the stillness and quiet of retreats like the Jesuit Center in Wernersville, Pennsylvania.
paragraphs.translationZh: 越来越多的人在宾夕法尼亚州韦纳斯维尔的耶稣会中心等静谧的静修所中休息一下。

paragraphs.sourceText: About a year ago, I flew to Singapore to join the writer Malcolm Gladwell, the fashion designer Marc Ecko and the graphic designer Stefan Sagmeister in addressing a group of advertising people on “Marketing to the Child of Tomorrow.” Soon after I arrived, the chief executive of the agency that had invited us took me aside. What he was most interested in, he began, was stillness and quiet.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大约一年前，我飞往新加坡，与作家马尔科姆·格拉德威尔 (Malcolm Gladwell)、时装设计师马克·埃科 (Marc Ecko) 和平面设计师斯特凡·萨格迈斯特 (Stefan Sagmeister) 一起，向一群广告人员发表了题为“面向明日之子的营销”的演讲。我到达后不久，邀请我们的机构的首席执行官把我拉到一边。他开始说，他最感兴趣的是静止和安静。

paragraphs.sourceText: A few months later, I read an interview with the well-known cutting-edge designer Philippe Starck.
paragraphs.translationZh: 几个月后，我读到了一篇对著名新锐设计师 Philippe Starck 的采访。

paragraphs.sourceText: What allowed him to remain so consistently ahead of the curve? “I never read any magazines or watch TV,” he said, perhaps with a little exaggeration. “Nor do I go to cocktail parties, dinners or anything like that.” He lived outside conventional ideas, he implied, because “I live alone mostly, in the middle of nowhere.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 是什么让他能够始终保持领先地位？ “我从不读任何杂志或看电视，”他说，也许有点夸张。 “我也不去参加鸡尾酒会、晚宴或类似的活动。”他暗示，他生活在传统观念之外，因为“我大部分时间都是独自生活，在一个偏僻的地方。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Around the same time, I noticed that those who part with $2,285 a night to stay in a cliff-top room at the Post Ranch Inn in Big Sur, California, pay partly for the privilege of not having a TV in their rooms; the future of travel, I’m reliably told, lies in “black-hole resorts,” which charge high prices precisely because you can’t get online in their rooms.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大约在同一时间，我注意到那些花 2,285 美元一晚住在加利福尼亚州大苏尔 Post Ranch Inn 悬崖顶房间的人，部分是为了享受房间里没有电视的特权；有人可靠地告诉我，旅行的未来在于“黑洞度假村”，这些度假村收取高价正是因为你无法在他们的房间里上网。

paragraphs.sourceText: Has it really come to this?
paragraphs.translationZh: 真的已经到了这个地步了吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: The more ways we have to connect, the more many of us seem desperate to unplug. Internet rescue camps in South Korea and China try to save kids addicted to the screen.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们拥有的联系方式越多，我们中的许多人似乎就越渴望拔掉电源。韩国和中国的互联网救援营试图拯救沉迷于屏幕的孩子。

paragraphs.sourceText: Writer friends of mine pay good money to get the Freedom software that enables them to disable the very Internet connections that seemed so emancipating not long ago. Even Intel experimented in 2007 with conferring four uninterrupted hours of quiet time (no phone or e-mail) every Tuesday morning on 300 engineers and managers. Workers were not allowed to use the phone or send e-mail, but simply had the chance to clear their heads and to hear themselves think.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我的作家朋友花了很多钱购买 Freedom 软件，使他们能够禁用不久前看起来如此解放的互联网连接。甚至英特尔也在 2007 年进行了实验，每周二早上为 300 名工程师和经理提供四个小时不间断的安静时间（不打电话或发送电子邮件）。工人们不被允许使用电话或发送电子邮件，但他们只是有机会清醒头脑并倾听自己的想法。

paragraphs.sourceText: The average American spends at least eight and a half hours a day in front of a screen, Nicholas Carr notes in his book The Shallows. The average American teenager sends or receives 75 text messages a day, though one girl managed to handle an average of 10,000 every 24 hours for a month.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尼古拉斯·卡尔在他的《浅滩》一书中指出，美国人平均每天至少花八个半小时在屏幕前。美国青少年平均每天发送或接收 75 条短信，但一名女孩一个月平均每 24 小时处理 10,000 条短信。

paragraphs.sourceText: Since luxury is a function of scarcity, the children of tomorrow will long for nothing more than intervals of freedom from all the blinking machines, streaming videos and scrolling headlines that leave them feeling empty and too full all at once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 由于奢侈是稀缺的结果，未来的孩子们所渴望的无非就是摆脱那些闪烁的机器、流媒体视频和滚动的头条新闻，这些让他们同时感到空虚和太充实。

paragraphs.sourceText: The urgency of slowing down—to find the time and space to think—is nothing new, of course, and wiser souls have always reminded us that the more attention we pay to the moment, the less time and energy we have to place it in some larger context. “Distraction is the only thing that consoles us for our miseries,” the French philosopher Blaise Pascal wrote in the 17th century, “and yet it is itself the greatest of our miseries.” He also famously remarked that all of man’s problems come from his inability to sit quietly in a room alone.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当然，放慢脚步的紧迫性——寻找时间和空间来思考——并不是什么新鲜事，聪明的灵魂总是提醒我们，我们越关注当下，我们就越不需要时间和精力把它放在更大的背景下。法国哲学家布莱斯·帕斯卡 (Blaise Pascal) 在 17 世纪写道：“分心是唯一能安慰我们痛苦的事情，但它本身就是我们最大的痛苦。”他还说过一句名言：人类的所有问题都源于他无法独自安静地坐在房间里。

paragraphs.sourceText: When telegraphs and trains brought in the idea that convenience was more important than content, Henry David Thoreau reminded us that “the man whose horse trots (奔跑), a mile in a minute does not carry the most important messages.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 当电报和火车带来便利比内容更重要的观念时，亨利·大卫·梭罗提醒我们，“骑马一分钟跑一英里的人并没有携带最重要的信息。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Marshall McLuhan, who came closer than most to seeing what was coming, warned, “When things come at you very fast, naturally you lose touch with yourself.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 马歇尔·麦克卢汉（Marshall McLuhan）比大多数人都更了解即将发生的事情，他警告说：“当事情来得非常快时，你自然会失去与自己的联系。”

paragraphs.sourceText: We have more and more ways to communicate, but less and less to say. Partly because we are so busy communicating. And we are rushing to meet so many deadlines that we hardly register that what we need most are lifelines.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们沟通的方式越来越多，可说的却越来越少。部分原因是我们太忙于沟通。我们急于赶在最后期限前完成任务，以至于我们几乎没有意识到我们最需要的是生命线。

paragraphs.sourceText: So what to do? More and more people I know seem to be turning to yoga, or meditation (沉思), or tai chi (太极)；these aren’t New Age fads (时尚的事物) so much as ways to connect with what could be called the wisdom of old age. Two friends of mine observe an “Internet sabbath (安息日)” every week, turning off their online connections from Friday night to Monday morning. Other friends take walks and “forget” their cellphones at home.
paragraphs.translationZh: 那么该怎么办呢？我认识的越来越多的人似乎转向瑜伽、冥想或太极；与其说这些是新时代的时尚，不如说是与所谓的老年智慧联系起来的方式。我的两个朋友每周都会过“安息日”，从周五晚上到周一早上都会关闭网络连接。其他朋友散步时“忘记”了手机在家。

paragraphs.sourceText: A series of tests in recent years has shown, Mr. Carr points out, that after spending time in quiet rural settings, subjects “exhibit greater attentiveness, stronger memory and generally improved 2 / 30 cognition. Their brains become both calmer and sharper.” More than that, empathy (同感，共鸣)， as well as deep thought, depends (as neuroscientists like Antonio Damasio have found) on neural processes that are “inherently slow.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 卡尔指出，近​​年来的一系列测试表明，在安静的乡村环境中度过一段时间后，受试者“表现出更集中的注意力、更强的记忆力和普遍改善的认知能力。他们的大脑变得更加平静和敏锐。”更重要的是，同感（同感，共鸣）以及深刻的思考（正如安东尼奥·达马西奥等神经科学家所发现的那样）依赖于“本质上缓慢”的神经过程。

paragraphs.sourceText: I turn to eccentric measures to try to keep my mind sober and ensure that I have time to do nothing at all (which is the only time when I can see what I should be doing the rest of the time). I have yet to use a cellphone and I have never Tweeted or entered Facebook. I try not to go online till my day’s writing is finished, and I moved from Manhattan to rural Japan in part so I could more easily survive for long stretches entirely on foot.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我采取一些古怪的措施来试图保持头脑清醒，并确保我有时间什么都不做（这是我唯一能看到其余时间应该做什么的时间）。我还没有使用过手机，也从未发过推文或进入过 Facebook。在完成一天的写作之前，我尽量不上网，我从曼哈顿搬到了日本乡村，部分原因是这样我可以更轻松地长时间完全步行生存。

paragraphs.sourceText: None of this is a matter of asceticism (苦行主义)；it is just pure selfishness. Nothing makes me feel better than being in one place, absorbed in a book, a conversation, or music. It is actually something deeper than mere happiness: it is joy, which the monk (僧侣) David Steindl-Rast describes as “that kind of happiness that doesn’t depend on what happens.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 这一切都不是苦行主义的问题，而只是纯粹的自私。没有什么比在一个地方专注于一本书、一场谈话或音乐更让我感觉更好的了。它实际上比单纯的幸福更深层次的东西：它是快乐，僧侣戴维·斯坦德尔-拉斯特（David Steindl-Rast）将其描述为“那种不依赖于发生的事情的幸福”。

paragraphs.sourceText: It is vital, of course, to stay in touch with the world. But it is only by having some distance from the world that you can see it whole, and understand what you should be doing with it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当然，与世界保持联系至关重要。但只有与世界保​​持一定的距离，你才能看到整个世界，并明白你应该用它做什么。

paragraphs.sourceText: For more than 20 years, therefore, I have been going several times a year—often for no longer than three days—to a Benedictine hermitage (修道院)，40 minutes down the road, as it happens, from the Post Ranch Inn. I don’t attend services when I am there, and I have never meditated, there or anywhere; I just take walks and read and lose myself in the stillness, recalling that it is only by stepping briefly away from my wife and bosses and friends that I will have anything useful to bring to them. The last time I was in the hermitage, three months ago, I happened to meet with a youngish-looking man with a 3-year-old boy around his shoulders.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，20多年来，我每年都会去几次——通常不超过三天——去一个本笃会隐修院，碰巧从波斯特牧场旅馆沿路走40分钟。我在那里时不参加礼拜，也从未在那里或任何地方冥想过；我只是散步、读书，沉浸在宁静中，回想起只有短暂离开我的妻子、老板和朋友，我才能给他们带来任何有用的东西。上次来闭关是三个月前，我碰巧遇到一个看上去很年轻的男人，肩上还抱着一个三岁的男孩。

paragraphs.sourceText: “You’re Pico, aren’t you?” the man said, and introduced himself as Larry; we had met, I gathered, 19 years before, when he had been living in the hermitage as an assistant to one of the monks.
paragraphs.translationZh: “你是皮可，不是吗？”那人说道，并介绍自己是拉里。据我所知，我们是在 19 年前认识的，当时他住在修道院里，担任一位僧侣的助手。

paragraphs.sourceText: “What are you doing now?” I asked.
paragraphs.translationZh: “你现在在做什么？”我问。

paragraphs.sourceText: We smiled. No words were necessary.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们笑了。无需多言。

paragraphs.sourceText: “I try to bring my kids here as often as I can,” he went on. The child of tomorrow, I realized, may actually be ahead of us, in terms of sensing not what is new, but what is essential.
paragraphs.translationZh: “我尽可能多地带我的孩子来这里，”他继续说道。我意识到，明天的孩子实际上可能走在我们的前面，他们不是在感知什么是新的，而是在感知什么是必要的。

paragraphs.sourceText: A key process in interpersonal interaction is that of social comparison, in that we evaluate ourselves in terms of how we compare to others. In particular, we engage in two types of comparison. First, we decide whether we are superior or inferior to others on certain dimensions, such as attractiveness, intelligence, popularity, etc. Here, the important aspect is to compare with an appropriate reference group. For example, modest joggers should not compare their performance with Olympic standard marathon (马拉松) runners. Second, we judge the extent to which we are the same as or different from others. At certain stages of life, especially adolescence, the pressure to be seen as similar to peers is immense. Thus, wearing the right brand of clothes or shoes may be of 8 / 30

the utmost importance. We also need to know whether our thoughts, beliefs and ideas are in line with those of other people. This is part of the process of self-validation whereby we employ self-disclosures to seek support for our self-concept.

People who do not have access to a good listener may not only be denied the opportunity to heighten their self-awareness, but they are also denied valuable feedback as to the validity and acceptability of their inner thoughts and feelings. By discussing these with others, we receive feedback as to whether these are experiences which others have as well, or whether they are less common. Furthermore, by gauging the reactions to our self-disclosures we learn what types are acceptable or unacceptable with particular people and in specific situations. On occasions it is the fear that certain disclosures may be unacceptable to family or friends that motivates an individual to seek professional help. Counsellors will be familiar with client statements such as: “I just couldn’t talk about this to my husband.”, “I really can’t let my mother know my true feelings.” Another aspect of social comparison in the counselling context relates to a technique known as normalising. This is the process whereby helpers provide reassurance to clients that what they are experiencing is not abnormal or atypical (非典型的), but is a normal reaction shared by others when facing such circumstances. Patient disclosure, facilitated by the therapist, seems also to facilitate the process of normalising.

paragraphs.sourceText: Amid all the job losses, there’s one category of worker that the economic disruption has been good for: nonhumans.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在所有失业中，有一类工人受益于经济动荡：非人类。

paragraphs.sourceText: From self-service checkout lines at the supermarket to industrial robots armed with saws and taught to carve up animal bodies in slaughter-houses, these ever-more-intelligent machines are now not just assisting workers but actually kicking them out of their jobs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 从超市的自助收银台到配备锯子并被教导在屠宰场切割动物尸体的工业机器人，这些越来越智能的机器现在不仅在帮助工人，而且实际上让他们失业。

paragraphs.sourceText: Automation isn’t just affecting factory workers, either. Some law firms now use artificial intelligence software to scan and read mountains of legal documents, work that previously was performed by highly-paid human lawyers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 自动化不仅仅影响工厂工人。一些律师事务所现在使用人工智能软件来扫描和阅读大量的法律文件，而这些工作以前是由高薪人类律师完成的。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Robots continue to have an impact on blue-collar jobs, and white-collar jobs are under attack by microprocessors,” says economics professor Edward Leamer. The recession permanently wiped out 2.5 million jobs. U.S. gross domestic product has climbed back to pre-recession levels, meaning we’re producing as much as before, only with 6% fewer workers. To be sure, robotics are not the only job killers out there, with outsourcing (外包) stealing far more jobs than automation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 经济学教授爱德华·利默（Edward Leamer）表示：“机器人继续对蓝领工作产生影响，而白领工作则受到微处理器的攻击。”经济衰退永久性地消灭了 250 万个工作岗位。美国的国内生产总值已回升至经济衰退前的水平，这意味着我们的生产量与以前一样多，只是工人数量减少了 6%。可以肯定的是，机器人并不是唯一的就业杀手，外包抢走了的就业岗位远多于自动化。

paragraphs.sourceText: Jeff Burnstein, president of the Robotics Industry Association, argues that robots actually save U.S. jobs. His logic: companies that embrace automation might use fewer workers, but that’s still better than firing everyone and moving the work overseas.
paragraphs.translationZh: 机器人工业协会主席杰夫伯恩斯坦认为，机器人实际上挽救了美国的就业机会。他的逻辑是：拥抱自动化的公司可能会使用更少的工人，但这仍然比解雇所有人并将工作转移到海外要好。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s not that robots are cheaper than humans, though often they are. It’s that they’re better. “In some cases the quality requirements are so exacting that even if you wanted to have a human do the job, you couldn’t,” Burnstein says.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这并不是说机器人比人类便宜，尽管事实往往如此。这是因为他们更好。 “在某些情况下，质量要求非常严格，即使你想让人来做这项工作，你也做不到，”伯恩斯坦说。

paragraphs.sourceText: Same goes for surgeons, who’re using robotic systems to perform an ever-growing list of operations—not because the machines save money but because, thanks to the greater precision of robots, the patients recover in less time and have fewer complications, says Dr. Myriam Curet.
paragraphs.translationZh: Myriam Curet 博士表示，对于外科医生来说也是如此，他们使用机器人系统执行越来越多的手术，不是因为机器省钱，而是因为机器人精度更高，患者可以在更短的时间内康复，并发症也更少。

paragraphs.sourceText: Surgeons may survive the robot invasion, but others at the hospital might not be so lucky, as iRobot, maker of the Roomba, a robot vacuum cleaner, has been showing off Ava, which could be used as a messenger in a hospital. And once you’re home, recovering, Ava could let you talk to your doctor, so there’s no need to send someone to your house. That “mobile telepresence” could be useful at the office. If you’re away on a trip, you can still attend a meeting. Just connect via videoconferencing software, so your face appears on Ava’s screen.
paragraphs.translationZh: 外科医生可能会在机器人入侵中幸存下来，但医院里的其他人可能就没那么幸运了，因为扫地机器人 Roomba 的制造商 iRobot 一直在展示 Ava，它可以在医院里用作信使。一旦您康复回家，Ava 可以让您与您的医生交谈，因此无需派人到您家。这种“移动远程呈现”在办公室可能很有用。如果您外出旅行，您仍然可以参加会议。只需通过视频会议软件连接，您的脸就会出现在 Ava 的屏幕上。

paragraphs.sourceText: Is any job safe? I was hoping to say “journalist,” but researchers are already developing software that can gather facts and write a news story. Which means that a few years from now, a robot could be writing this column. And who will read it? Well, there might be a lot of us hanging around with lots of free time on our hands.

paragraphs.sourceText: You’ve now heard it so many times, you can probably repeat it in your sleep. President Obama will no doubt make the point publicly when he gets to Beijing: the Chinese need to consume more; they need—believe it or not—to become more like Americans, for the sake of the global economy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 你现在已经听过很多次了，你可能会在睡梦中重复它。奥巴马总统到访北京时无疑会公开表明这一点：中国人需要增加消费；不管你信不信，为了全球经济，他们需要变得更像美国人。

paragraphs.sourceText: And it’s all true. But the other side of that equation is that the U.S. needs to save more. For the moment, American households actually are doing so. After the personal-savings rate dipped to zero in 2005, the shock of the economic crisis last year prompted people to snap shut their wallets.

paragraphs.sourceText: In China, the household-savings rate exceeds 20%. It is partly for policy reasons. As we’ve seen, wage earners are expected to care for not only their children but their aging parents. And there is, to date, only the flimsiest (脆弱的) of publicly-funded health care and pension systems, which increases incentives for individuals to save while they are working. But China is a society that has long esteemed personal financial prudence (谨慎). There is no chance that will change anytime soon, even if the government creates a better social safety net and successfully encourages greater consumer spending.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在中国，家庭储蓄率超过20%。部分原因是政策原因。正如我们所看到的，工薪阶层不仅要照顾自己的孩子，还要照顾年迈的父母。迄今为止，只有最脆弱的公共资助的医疗保健和养老金制度，这增加了个人在工作时储蓄的动力。但中国是一个历来推崇个人理财的社会。即使政府建立了更好的社会安全网并成功地鼓励了更多的消费支出，这种情况也不可能很快改变。

paragraphs.sourceText: Why does the U.S. need to learn a little frugality (节俭)？Because healthy savings rates are one of the surest indicators of a country’s long-term financial health. High savings lead, over time, to increased investment, which in turn generates productivity gains, innovation and job growth. In short, savings are the seed corn of a good economic harvest.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为什么美国需要学会一点节俭？因为健康的储蓄率是一个国家长期财务健康最可靠的指标之一。随着时间的推移，高储蓄会导致投资增加，进而带来生产力提高、创新和就业增长。总之，储蓄是经济丰收的种子。

paragraphs.sourceText: The U.S. government thus needs to act as well. By running constant deficits, it is dis-saving, even as households save more. Peter Orszag, Obama’s Budget Director, recently called the U.S. budget deficits unsustainable and he’s right. To date, the U.S. has seemed unable to see the consequences of spending so much more than is taken in. That needs to change. And though Hu Jintao and the rest of the Chinese leadership aren’t inclined to lecture visiting Presidents, he might gently hint that Beijing is getting a little nervous about the value of the dollar—which has fallen 15% since March, in large part because of increasing fears that America’s debt load is becoming unmanageable.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，美国政府也需要采取行动。即使家庭储蓄更多，持续的赤字也会阻碍储蓄。奥巴马预算主任彼得·奥尔萨格最近称美国预算赤字不可持续，他是对的。迄今为止，美国似乎还看不到支出超过吸收的后果。这种情况需要改变。尽管胡锦涛和其他中国领导层不愿意对来访的国家领导人说教，但他可能会温和地暗示，北京方面对美元的价值有些紧张——自3月份以来，美元已经下跌了15%，很大程度上是因为人们越来越担心美国的债务负担变得难以控制。

paragraphs.sourceText: That’s what happens when you’re the world’s biggest creditor: you get to drop hints like that, which would be enough by themselves to create international economic chaos if they were ever leaked. (Every time any official in Beijing deliberates publicly about seeking an alternative to the U.S. dollar for the $2.1 trillion China holds in reserve, currency traders have a heart attack.) If Americans saved more and spent less, consistently over time, they wouldn’t have to worry about all that.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当你是世界上最大的债权人时，就会发生这种情况：你可以发出这样的暗示，如果这些暗示被泄露，这些暗示本身就足以造成国际经济混乱。 （每当北京的官员公开考虑为中国持有的 2.1 万亿美元外汇储备寻找美元的替代品时，外汇交易员就会心脏病发作。）如果美国人随着时间的推移持续增加储蓄，减少支出，他们就不必担心这一切。

options.sourceText: Providing fewer incentives for saving.
options.reflowSourceText: Providing fewer incentives for saving.
options.translationZh: 提供较少的储蓄激励。

options.sourceText: Improving China’s social security system.
options.reflowSourceText: Improving China’s social security system.
options.translationZh: 完善中国社会保障体系。

options.sourceText: Cutting down the expenses on child-rearing.
options.reflowSourceText: Cutting down the expenses on child-rearing.
options.translationZh: 减少抚养孩子的开支。

options.sourceText: The more one saves, the more returns one will reap.
options.reflowSourceText: The more one saves, the more returns one will reap.
options.translationZh: 一个人储蓄越多，获得的回报就越多。

options.sourceText: A country’s economy hinges on its savings policy.
options.reflowSourceText: A country’s economy hinges on its savings policy.
options.translationZh: 一个国家的经济取决于其储蓄政策。

options.sourceText: Those who keep saving will live an easy life in the end.
options.reflowSourceText: Those who keep saving will live an easy life in the end.
options.translationZh: 那些坚持储蓄的人最终会过上轻松的生活。

options.sourceText: A healthy savings rate promotes economic prosperity.
options.reflowSourceText: A healthy savings rate promotes economic prosperity.
options.translationZh: 健康的储蓄率可以促进经济繁荣。

options.sourceText: When Beijing allows its currency exchange rates to float.
options.reflowSourceText: When Beijing allows its currency exchange rates to float.
options.translationZh: 当北京允许其货币汇率浮动时。

options.sourceText: When China starts to reduce its current foreign reserves.
options.reflowSourceText: When China starts to reduce its current foreign reserves.
options.translationZh: 当中国开始减少目前的外汇储备时。

options.sourceText: When China talks about switching its dollar reserves to other currencies.
options.reflowSourceText: When China talks about switching its dollar reserves to other currencies.
options.translationZh: 当中国谈论将其美元储备转向其他货币时。

options.sourceText: When Beijing mentions in public the huge debts America owes China.
options.reflowSourceText: When Beijing mentions in public the huge debts America owes China.
options.translationZh: 当北京公开提及美国欠中国的巨额债务时。

options.sourceText: To urge the American government to cut deficits.
options.reflowSourceText: To urge the American government to cut deficits.
options.translationZh: 敦促美国政府削减赤字。

options.sourceText: To encourage Chinese people to spend more.
options.reflowSourceText: To encourage Chinese people to spend more.
options.translationZh: 鼓励中国人多花钱。

options.sourceText: To tell Americans not to worry about their economy.
options.reflowSourceText: To tell Americans not to worry about their economy.
options.translationZh: 告诉美国人不要担心他们的经济。

options.sourceText: To promote understanding between China and America.
options.reflowSourceText: To promote understanding between China and America.
options.translationZh: 促进中美之间的了解。
